title: Introduce Batchsmith presets assembler and manifest bundler
author: Avery Collins
body:
Motivation: operational teams and tenant onboarding pipelines repeatedly construct fragile combinations of batching defaults, cache presets and quantization profiles. Small mismatches in keys or ordering led to silent unit-economics regressions during rollout. This PR adds a deterministic assembler (batchsmith presets assembler) that consolidates tenant defaults, workload hints, and quant profiles into a single versioned manifest that the serving runtime and Console CLI can consume.

What this change does:
- Implements a new CLI command `redwood batchsmith assemble` that produces a canonical manifest.json from a directory of inputs (tenant-defaults/, quant-profiles/, batch-presets/). The assembler performs schema validation, deterministic key normalization, and content-addressed manifest versioning (sha256).
- Adds a lightweight library package `pkg/presets/assembler` used by the CLI and the onboarding server to avoid duplication. The assembler exposes a dry-run mode and a `--fail-on-cost-regression` flag that runs a fast unit-econ estimator to detect immediate regressions compared to a baseline manifest.
- Introduces snapshot tests for manifest entropy and two migration helpers: a v1->v2 normalizer that flattens legacy batch shape fields, and a compatibility shim for older quant profiles.
- Adds examples and docs: `docs/presets/assembler.md` with usage, examples and recommended CI gating steps.

Design notes:
- Determinism: manifests are canonicalized by stable key ordering and whitespace normalization; the final manifest includes a `manifest_hash` and `source_inventory` block for traceability (source_inventory is a list of input file hashes). This enables reproducible CI checks and smaller diff footprints for human reviews.
- Cost safety: the `--fail-on-cost-regression` runs a conservative token-cost estimator (approx) using stored unit-cost coefficients so infra and SRE can gate merges that increase per-token cost beyond a threshold.
- Rollout: CLI emits a `manifest:v2` that the Console and Dedicated onboarding components can opt into; older runtimes fallback to the compatibility shim. We keep both formats in S3 for 30 days to enable rollbacks.

Checklist: [x] unit tests for assembler internals, [x] integration test for CLI assemble -> manifest load, [x] e2e smoke run against staging runtime with compatibility shim, [x] docs updated, [x] added snapshot fixtures, [x] telemetry metrics (assembler.duration, assembler.rejections).

Testing notes:
- Local: `make test-presets` runs unit and snapshot checks.
- CI: initial integration job failed flakily in staging e2e; I narrowed the race to the staging onboarding server startup and added a 5s readiness probe in the e2e harness. All CI jobs pass now.

Migration & rollout plan:
1) Merge assembler and land CLI in Canary build.
2) Add a small dry-run job in existing tenant onboarding pipeline to emit manifests and compare hashes for 48h.
3) If stable, flip the onboarding server toggle to accept manifest:v2 and start using the assembled manifest directly.
4) Deprecate manual ad-hoc preset uploads and run a final cleanup job to convert remaining legacy entries to manifest:v2.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: accidental cost regressions. Mitigation: `--fail-on-cost-regression` and CI gating + telemetry.
- Risk: schema drift. Mitigation: Canary rollout and help text in CLI plus migration normalizer included here.

Notes for reviewers: focus on assembler deterministic behavior (pkg/presets/assembler/assemble.go) and the cost-estimator stub (pkg/presets/econ_estimator.go). The CLI glue is intentionally minimal and delegates to the library so behaviour stays the same across consumers.

Related: ENG-4123 tracks CI gating requirements; ENG-4170 tracks Console integration tasks.
commits: a1f9d2c: initial assembler library and canonicalizer
b2d4e7a: add CLI glue and dry-run/cost-regression flag
c3e8f01: add snapshot fixtures and v1->v2 normalizer
d4f9e1a: docs, e2e readiness probe and telemetry metrics
e5a12b3: fix flaky e2e by adding readiness retry and tests
review_comments: Diego Ramirez: Can we avoid embedding costs in the manifest itself? Suggest keeping cost coefficients external and reference them by id so manifests remain immutable.

Avery Collins: Reply: agreed. Implemented a `cost_profile_ref` field and moved the coefficients into /presets/cost-profiles/; assembler resolves refs during dry-run only — manifest stays versioned and immutable.
Priya Shah: Tested locally, but noticed the normalizer drops an optional `max_batch_tokens` field for some tenants. Please add a unit test that preserves unknown fields or migrates safely.
Avery Collins: Reply: added preserveUnknown flag in normalizer and explicit migration path for `max_batch_tokens`. Added tests to snapshot fixtures. Thanks Priya.
Liam O'Connor: Approve after a couple minor nits on godoc comments and adding CLI examples in the README.
ci_checks: integration: pass (assemble -> load manifest against staging runtime)
e2e: pass (staging onboarding harness, readiness retry added)
release_notes: Introduce Batchsmith presets assembler CLI and library: deterministic manifest generation, dry-run cost regression checks, migration normalizer, and docs. Backwards compatible via compatibility shim.
